channel.title: Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Massachusetts and RI Lawyers Weekly (masslawyersweekly.com)

item.title: Civil practice – Commitment
item.description: Where a civil commitment order has been challenged on appeal, the order must be vacated because there was insufficient evidence to support a finding of a likelihood of serious harm.

item.title: Civil practice – Commitment – Substance use disorder
item.description: Where a respondent has appealed from a commitment order, that order should be affirmed because the evidence was sufficient to establish that the respondent had a substance use disorder, that she posed a likelihood of serious harm to herself, and that there was no less restrictive alternative to commitment.

item.title: Search and seizure – Storage unit
item.description: Where a defendant has moved to suppress evidence found in an interior storage unit during the execution of a search warrant at 34 Shattuck Street in Lawrence, his motion should be denied because officers did not exceed the scope of the warrant when they searched the storage unit.

item.title: Commercial – Trade secrets
item.description: Where a plaintiff has requested a preliminary injunction barring two defendants from using her trade secrets, that request should be denied because the plaintiff has not shown a reasonable likelihood that she will be able to prove that either defendant misused confidential material that was developed in her laboratory.

item.title: Civil practice – Impoundment
item.description: Where impoundment has been requested, that request should be denied because the parties have not identified any trade secrets or other highly sensitive information that may properly be withheld from the public file.

item.title: Constitutional – Immunity – 11th Amendment
item.description: Where (1) the Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management directed the plaintiff, as operator of the Flat River Reservoir Dam, to reduce the dam’s water flow and (2) the plaintiff then brought suit alleging federal constitutional violations, the dismissal of those counts should be upheld based on the lower court’s two well-reasoned opinions cogently explaining why each of the counts fails to state a plausible claim for relief.

item.title: Immigration – Credibility – Death threats
item.description: Where claims for asylum, withholding of removal, and protection under the Convention Against Torture were dismissed based on an adverse credibility finding, a remand must be ordered because (1) it was error to ignore potentially important documentary and testimonial evidence and (2) an incorrect standard was applied to the withholding of removal claim.

item.title: Search and seizure – Emergency – Warrantless entry
item.description: Where a defendant convicted of sex trafficking of a minor has challenged the denial of his motion to suppress evidence found during a warrantless search, that challenge lacks merit, as law enforcement officers had an objectively reasonable basis to conclude that an emergency existed and that the place they sought to search was reasonably linked to the perceived emergency.

item.title: Immigration – Nexus – Waiver
item.description: Where applications for asylum and withholding of removal were denied on the ground that the applicant had failed to show the required nexus between the harm she experienced and her asserted protected status, the applicant’s petition for review must be denied because of her failure to make any developed argument as to why the nexus determination was incorrect.

item.title: Federal judge allows Live Nation antitrust lawsuit over concert monopoly to proceed
item.description: A federal judge denied Live Nation's bid to dismiss an antitrust lawsuit accusing it of monopolizing live concert ticketing and promotion markets.
